config.title: useSyncExternalStore

intro.title: useSyncExternalStore
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue component that displays a real-time counter. You will learn how to use the useSyncExternalStore hook to subscribe to an external data store and keep your component's state in sync with it. This involves creating a store, subscribing to changes, and updating the component's UI automatically. You'll work with Vue's reactivity system and JavaScript to manage external state effectively.
intro.usecase: In real-world Vue applications, useSyncExternalStore is essential for connecting Vue components to external state sources like browser APIs, third-party libraries, or WebSocket connections. For example, in a live dashboard monitoring system, you'd use it to sync real-time data feeds from external services with your Vue components, ensuring the UI updates instantly when new data arrives. This pattern is also crucial in collaborative tools like shared document editors, where it synchronizes external cursor positions or selection states across multiple users. Developers implement this when building financial trading platforms, real-time analytics dashboards, or any application that needs to react to changes outside the Vue reactivity system.

objectives: Initialize a Vue component with useSyncExternalStore to subscribe to an external data source
Configure a custom store with getSnapshot and subscribe methods compatible with useSyncExternalStore
Manipulate external store state and observe reactive updates in your Vue component
Implement cleanup logic to unsubscribe from external stores when components unmount
Integrate useSyncExternalStore with Vue's reactive system to display synchronized data
Construct a complete data flow between an external store and multiple Vue components
Apply useSyncExternalStore patterns to synchronize with browser APIs or third-party libraries

steps.title: Import Vue and useSyncExternalStore from Vue
steps.instruction: Import Vue and useSyncExternalStore from the 'vue' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both Vue and useSyncExternalStore from 'vue'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: importing multiple items from a package
import { createApp, ref } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary Vue APIs are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: Vue and useSyncExternalStore are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both Vue and useSyncExternalStore from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import both Vue and useSyncExternalStore from the 'vue' package.

steps.title: Create a simple external store
steps.instruction: Create a simple external store object named 'counterStore' with 'subscribe' and 'getSnapshot' methods. Define it as a plain JavaScript object with these two methods.
steps.hint: An external store is just a plain object that provides a way to subscribe to changes and get the current value. You can define it with object literal syntax.
steps.seedCode:
// Import Vue and useSyncExternalStore from 'vue'

// Create a simple external store object named 'counterStore' with subscribe and getSnapshot methods
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a 'counterStore' object with both required methods defined.
successCriteria: The 'counterStore' object exists and has both 'subscribe' and 'getSnapshot' methods defined.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure 'counterStore' has both 'subscribe' and 'getSnapshot' methods defined as functions.
steps.feedbackWrong: Please create a 'counterStore' object with 'subscribe' and 'getSnapshot' methods. Both should be defined as functions.

steps.title: Initialize the Vue component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named 'CounterDisplay' with a setup function that returns an empty object.
steps.hint: In Vue, a component can be defined as a function that returns an object from its setup function.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Vue component named CounterDisplay is created with a setup function that returns an empty object.
successCriteria: The component is named 'CounterDisplay' and has a setup function that returns an object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named 'CounterDisplay' and the setup function returns an object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't set up correctly. Check that you've named it 'CounterDisplay' and the setup function returns an object.

steps.title: Use useSyncExternalStore to connect to the store
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function of your CounterDisplay component, call useSyncExternalStore and pass it the subscribe and getSnapshot methods from counterStore. Store the result in a variable named count.
steps.hint: useSyncExternalStore takes two arguments: a subscribe function and a getSnapshot function. You can call it like: const count = useSyncExternalStore(counterStore.subscribe, counterStore.getSnapshot);
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: Using useSyncExternalStore in a Vue component setup
const count = useSyncExternalStore(counterStore.subscribe, counterStore.getSnapshot);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have access to the current value from counterStore through the count variable.
successCriteria: useSyncExternalStore is called inside the setup function with counterStore.subscribe and counterStore.getSnapshot as arguments, and the result is stored in a variable named count.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling useSyncExternalStore with both arguments: subscribe and getSnapshot from counterStore, and storing the result in a variable named count.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. Inside the setup function, you need to call useSyncExternalStore(counterStore.subscribe, counterStore.getSnapshot) and store the result in a variable named count.

steps.title: Return the store value from setup
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, return an object that makes the store value available to the template. The object should have a property named 'count' whose value is the result of the useSyncExternalStore call.
steps.hint: The setup function should return an object like { count: storeValue }. This will expose 'count' to the template.
steps.expectedOutcome: The setup function now returns an object with a 'count' property, making the store value accessible in the template.
successCriteria: The setup function returns an object containing a property named 'count' whose value is the result of the useSyncExternalStore call.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning an object with a property named 'count' that holds the store value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The setup function should return an object with a 'count' property containing the store value. Check your return statement.

steps.title: Add the template section
steps.instruction: Add a template section to your component that returns a single div element.
steps.hint: In Vue single-file components, the template section defines the HTML structure. Add a template tag with a div inside.
steps.analogousExample: // Example template section
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a template section with a div element, ready to display content.
successCriteria: The component includes a template section with a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added both the template tag and a div element inside it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template section is missing or incomplete. Add a template tag with a div element inside.

steps.title: Display the store value in the template
steps.instruction: In the template section, use interpolation to display the storeValue returned from setup.
steps.hint: In Vue templates, you can display reactive values using double curly braces {{ }}. The storeValue is already available in the template because it's returned from setup.
steps.analogousExample: // Displaying a reactive value in template
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will show the current store value (0 initially) when rendered.
successCriteria: The template contains interpolation {{ storeValue }} to display the reactive store value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the exact variable name 'storeValue' in the interpolation.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template should display the storeValue using Vue's interpolation syntax {{ storeValue }}.

steps.title: Add a button to increment the store value
steps.instruction: Add a button element inside the template's div that, when clicked, increments the counterStore.value by 1.
steps.hint: Use the <button> tag and add a @click handler that modifies counterStore.value directly.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with click handler
<button @click="counterStore.value++">Increment</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will contain a button that increments the store value when clicked.
successCriteria: A button element with @click handler that increments counterStore.value is added to the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has a @click handler that increments counterStore.value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or doesn't have the correct click handler to increment the store value.

steps.title: Implement the increment handler
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, create a function named increment that updates the counterStore.value by 1 and calls the store's callback to notify subscribers.
steps.hint: The increment function should increase counterStore.value and then call counterStore.callback() if it exists.
steps.expectedOutcome: The increment function is defined in setup and properly updates the external store's state.
successCriteria: A function named increment is created that increments counterStore.value and calls counterStore.callback().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your increment function both increases counterStore.value and calls counterStore.callback() to notify subscribers.
steps.feedbackWrong: The increment handler isn't quite right. Remember to create a function that updates counterStore.value and calls the callback.

steps.title: Test the reactive store updates
steps.instruction: Click the increment button in the browser preview and observe the displayed value update.
steps.hint: The button should already be wired to increment the store value. Click it and watch the number increase.
steps.analogousExample:
// Testing reactive updates
// After clicking the button, the displayed value should increase by 1 each time
steps.expectedOutcome: When you click the increment button, the displayed value should increase from 0 to 1, then 2, etc., demonstrating that useSyncExternalStore properly syncs the component with external store changes.
successCriteria: The component reacts to button clicks by updating the displayed store value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: The value might not be updating. Make sure the increment function properly updates counterStore.value and calls the stored callback.
steps.feedbackWrong: The value isn't updating. Check that the button's @click is wired to the increment function and that the store's subscribe/getSnapshot logic is correct.
